newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh grain harvest 11 mln T so far, 90 pct over.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh grain harvest 11 mln T so far, 90 pct over.

text.p: Kazakhstan has harvested a net 11 million tonnes of grain so far, with around 90 percent of the former Soviet republic's sown area gathered, an Agriculture Ministry spokesman said on Monday.
"Around 90 percent of the sown area has been gathered, and the harvest so far stands at around 11 million tonnes," Alexander Korablin told Reuters in the capital Almaty.
Last year's drought-hit harvest was officially around 10 million tonnes.
Korablin said rain and snow in Kazakhstan's northern grain belt had affected a portion of this year's harvest.
The bad weather meant that around 30 percent of grain in the north had not yet been harvested and much of it was under snow.
Kazakhstan's harvest had also been hit by a lack of equipment, spare parts and fuel.
Earlier this year, the government revised down its 1996 harvest forecast to 16.5 million tonnes from 18 million.
Korablin said last month that he expected the harvest to total 13-14 million tonnes.
Harvest estimates in the former Soviet republic are often underestimated as farmers, fearing they might be forced to sell to the state at low prices, deliberately mislead statisticians.
